elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Array shall ..." — expressly covers both expiry and termination (curing the one-way, termination-only scope of the 14.2 chapeau).

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: The insertion commits Array only to "a period of at least ninety (90) days"; no six-month assistance period appears anywhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: No pricing basis is stated for Array's assistance; the words "then-current rates" do not appear (deliberately omitted at fallback).

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to Ono all Data and other information belonging to, supplied by or processed for Ono that is in Array's possession."

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: The delivery obligation specifies no format; "commonly used, machine-readable format" language was omitted.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion or written certification obligation on Array appears; 14.2(a)(vi) runs only against Ono in respect of Array Product Materials and Confidential Information.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason" — both triggers expressly named in the operative sentence.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "(A) at Ono's request, provide transition assistance to Ono for a period of at least ninety (90) days following such expiration or termination" — the request condition attaches to every covered expiry or termination, not merely anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "(B) within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to Ono all Data and other information belonging to, supplied by or processed for Ono that is in Array's possession" — deadline runs from the termination/expiry event, not from a request.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Duplicate-scope note: the preferred six-month duration is unmet; only the 90-day fallback duration is granted.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the single inserted paragraph supplies the expiry-or-termination trigger, at least 90 days of Array-side transition assistance, and a 30-day export/delivery deadline running from the termination or expiry event itself.
Preferred level is not reached and is correctly not claimed: no six-month period, no then-current-rates basis, no machine-readable format, and no certification of deletion after return.

Minimality holds — one concise insertion into the termination article, no deletions, no re-wording of the existing one-way obligations in 14.2(a)(iv), (vi) or (ix), and no extras (no survival tail, at-own-expense wording, escrow, procedure or remedies language) beyond the three fallback elements.

Intent is preserved: Ono's existing wind-down duties (study transition, Regulatory Filing assignment, customer-data hand-over, return/destruction of Array Materials) all survive unchanged, and the new clause creates a reciprocal Array obligation rather than cutting back any Array right.

Drafting risk to repair (placement, not substance): the new paragraph is appended un-numbered at the end of Section 14.2, whose chapeau reads "In case of termination of this Agreement by either Party, this Section 14.2 shall apply". Although the inserted sentence carries its own "expiration or termination" trigger, give it a standalone number outside 14.2 (e.g. a new Section 14.5) or open it "Notwithstanding the introductory sentence of Section 14.2," so Array cannot argue the chapeau confines it to termination only.

Optional tightening if we push toward preferred: add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to limb (B) and a certification-of-deletion limb; add "at Array's then-current rates" only if Array resists uncompensated assistance.
